title: Narrioch (Gravesend Neck)
summary: Narrioch is a Kings County placename associated with Gravesend Neck, interpreted as a point or corner of land. The name is tied to the same 1654 release that names Mannahanning.
map_geometry_source: approximate modern Gravesend Neck marker, offset slightly from nearby Gravesend Neck placename for map visibility; not exact historical coordinate
history_content: Narrioch belongs to the Gravesend Neck landscape in present-day Brooklyn. It is closely related to Mannahanning / Coney Island, with time-specific documentary context shown through Historic Moments.
translation_content:
Narrioch is interpreted as a point of land or corner land, connecting the form with language for a point or corner and a land/place ending. Related spellings include Narriock and Narrioch.

Why Place Names Matter

“Thus, through geographical names, we can learn about geography, society, construction, history and culture of a region or country.”

— Le Minh Tam, Preserving and promoting the historical-cultural value of geographical names (2015), UNGEGN Information Bulletin No. 48, PDF page 17
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is an approximate general point for Gravesend Neck in Brooklyn, offset slightly from another Gravesend Neck placename marker for map visibility and is not an exact boundary for the older neck landscape.
